Forensic Cash Quality & Balance Sheet Fortress Assessment

PacBio generated $40.56M in revenue and reduced GAAP OpEx to $50.47M. Net quarterly cash burn of -$37.47M reflected Operating Cash Flow of -$34.87M and CapEx of $2.60M. Deducting non-cash stock compensation of $8.00M yields True Economic Free Cash Flow of $-45.47M.

• Cash & Investments Runway: Total cash and investments of $199.4M provides runway into late 2027 as restructuring actions continue to lower cash burn toward -$20M quarterly.
• Restructuring Payoff: Elimination of short-read commercial infrastructure reduced annualized overhead by over $75M.
• Convertible Debt Structure: Convertible senior notes of $643.1M carry favorable maturities through 2028-2030, avoiding immediate refinancing friction.
Row 4: Operational Wins, Drags & Earnings Call Q&A Audit
QUALITATIVE & TRANSCRIPT FORENSICS

Operational Wins & Catalysts

  • Consumables Blowout: High-margin consumables revenue rose +23.5% YoY to $20.80M, beating estimates by +$2.60M.
  • Vega System Adoption: Placed 35 benchtop Vega systems in the quarter, validating demand from regional academic centers.
  • OpEx Rationalization: Total GAAP operating expenses dropped to $50.47M, down from $54.78M in Q3 2025 and $66.99M in Q1 2026.
  • Revenue Guidance Narrowed: Full-year revenue narrowed to $155M-$160M, removing worst-case downside scenarios.

Execution Drags & Watch Items

  • CFO Jim Gibson Transition: Executive transition adds management uncertainty while search for permanent commercial CFO proceeds.
  • Capital Equipment Delays: Instrument revenue slipped -11.4% QoQ to $13.20M as academic customers navigate grant release timing.
  • Revio System Placements: Placed 15 Revio systems in Q3 vs 24 in Q2, reflecting macroeconomic caution on high-capital equipment.
  • Convertible Debt Overhang: $643.1M in convertible debt requires sustained execution to reach 2028 cash flow breakeven.

Top Institutional Analyst Q&A and Analyst Questions Forensic Exchanges

Dan Arias (Stifel) Consumables Surging to $20.8M & Revio Installed Base Utilization

Question: Christian, consumables came in very strong at $20.8M, up 23.5% YoY. Are you seeing an inflection in utilization across your population genomics customers, and how should we project Revio pull-through heading into 2027?

Executive Answer: Christian Henry (CEO) answered: 'Our consumable revenue of $20.8M was driven by record HiFi sequencing volume. As customers scaled their projects with our new SPRQ chemistry and larger genome initiatives like Verily and TychoBio gained momentum, sample throughput reached all-time highs. We expect consumable pull-through to remain durable as customers transition from validation to full production.'

Subbu Nambi (Guggenheim) Cash Burn Trajectory & Path to 2028 Breakeven

Question: With cash and investments at $199.4M and quarterly operating burn at $34.9M, can you walk us through the cadence of expense reductions that get PacBio to cash flow breakeven without external financing?

Executive Answer: Christian Henry responded: 'We have executed structural restructuring that eliminated over $75M in annualized operating costs, reflected in our OpEx coming down to $50.5M this quarter. As Vega shipments scale and gross margins expand toward 40% with higher consumable attach, our quarterly cash burn will decline sequentially toward -$20M in 2027 and reach breakeven by 2028. We are fully focused on managing our $199.4M liquidity fortress.'

Kyle Mikson (Canaccord Genuity) CFO Transition & Executive Stability

Question: Christian, regarding the announcement that Jim Gibson is stepping down as CFO to take an advisory role, can you give context on the transition timing and what qualifications you are prioritizing in the next finance chief?

Executive Answer: Christian Henry stated: 'Jim has been a terrific partner through our restructuring and asset rationalization. With our major cost-cutting programs implemented and the company on a stabilized operational footing, Jim and the board felt this was the natural time to transition. Jim will remain actively advising through March 2027, ensuring a seamless handover while we conduct a comprehensive search for our next commercial-phase CFO.'

Matt Sykes (Goldman Sachs) SPRQ-Nx Chemistry Adoption & Sequencing Cost Curve

Question: Christian, with the commercial introduction of SPRQ chemistry, how are your high-throughput Revio customers reacting to the lower price per genome, and is that driving elasticity in new customer segments?

Executive Answer: Christian Henry responded: 'SPRQ chemistry has been enthusiastically received because it lowers consumable run costs while boosting Q30+ data accuracy. We are seeing immediate elasticity as existing accounts ramp sample cohorts that were previously cost-prohibitive. That directly drove our $20.8M consumable delivery this quarter and expands our competitive moat against short-read alternatives.'
